name: Rootstock
tagline: Precision agriculture that fits in your pocket, not your budget
description: Rootstock builds affordable precision agriculture sensors designed for small and mid-size farms. Our solar-powered soil probes, weather stations, and crop health monitors cost a fraction of enterprise systems — delivering the same data-driven insights that industrial farms rely on to family operations and specialty growers.
mission:
The precision agriculture revolution has been happening for a decade, but it's been a revolution for the top 2%. Massive operations running $300K combine harvesters with GPS-guided autosteer and satellite imagery subscriptions. Meanwhile, the 2 million small farms in America — the ones growing your tomatoes at the farmers market, the ones experimenting with regenerative practices — are still guessing when to irrigate and hoping the frost holds off.

Rootstocks exists to democratize farm data. We build rugged, solar-powered sensor networks that any farmer can install in an afternoon. Soil moisture, temperature, pH, nitrogen levels, microclimate weather data — all streaming to a phone app that speaks plain English, not agronomy jargon. When your south field is trending dry, you get a text. When conditions are right for blight, you know before you see it.

We price our hardware at cost and charge a modest subscription for the intelligence layer. A full 40-acre deployment costs less than a single precision ag consultation from the big players. We believe this is the only way to actually reach the farmers who need this technology most — the ones operating on thin margins who can't afford to gamble on a bad season.

Our founding team includes a third-generation Iowa farmer, a hardware engineer from John Deere, and a soil scientist from UC Davis. We've lived the problem from every angle. We know that the best sensor in the world is worthless if it breaks in a hailstorm, if the battery dies in January, or if the dashboard requires a PhD to interpret.

The future of farming is data-informed, not data-overwhelmed. Rootstock is building the infrastructure to make every acre smarter — starting with the farms that feed your community, not just the ones that feed the commodity markets.
marketResearch:
The global precision agriculture market reached $9.4B in 2025 and is projected to hit $18.6B by 2030 at 14.6% CAGR. However, adoption remains concentrated among large-scale commodity operations (1,000+ acres). Farms under 200 acres — which represent 91% of US farms — have less than 8% precision ag adoption, creating a massive underserved segment worth an estimated $3.2B in the US alone.

Rootstock's serviceable addressable market focuses on specialty crop growers, organic farms, and small diversified operations in North America and Western Europe. These 1.8 million farms spend approximately $2.1B annually on crop management tools and services. Our initial SOM targets direct-to-consumer farms, CSA operations, and specialty growers in the Midwest, Pacific Northwest, and Northeast — roughly $280M in near-term opportunity.

The competitive landscape includes enterprise players like Trimble, John Deere Operations Center, and Climate Corp (Bayer), all priced for large operations at $5-15/acre/year. Budget options like Davis Instruments offer basic weather stations without intelligence. Emerging competitors include Arable (crop monitoring) and CropX (soil sensing), but both target mid-market at premium pricing. Rootstock differentiates through radical affordability ($1.50/acre/year), zero-maintenance solar hardware, and an app designed for farmers who don't self-identify as tech-forward.

Early traction includes 340 farms across 12 states in a beta program, with 87% monthly active usage — unusually high for agricultural IoT. Our hardware-at-cost model drives subscription retention of 93% annually. Distribution partnerships with rural co-ops and farm supply stores provide a capital-efficient channel that enterprise ag-tech companies have ignored.

name: Mise
tagline: Every ingredient, prepped and portioned. Just cook.
description: Mise delivers pre-measured, pre-prepped ingredients for adventurous home cooks who want to make restaurant-quality meals without spending 45 minutes on knife work. Unlike traditional meal kits, Mise lets you choose your own recipes — we just handle the tedious prep so you can focus on the joy of cooking.
mission:
The meal kit industry got one thing right and everything else wrong. They proved people want help getting dinner on the table. But they also proved that most home cooks don't want to be told what to eat, don't want a subscription they forget to pause, and definitely don't want to pay $14 per serving for a recipe they could have found on YouTube.

Mise takes a different approach. We're not a meal kit company — we're a prep kitchen. You tell us what you're making this week (or browse our recipe library for inspiration), and we deliver every ingredient washed, chopped, measured, and organized. Onions diced. Garlic minced. Spices pre-measured into labeled packets. Proteins trimmed and portioned. Your mise en place, done.

We exist because the real barrier to cooking isn't skill or desire — it's the 30-45 minutes of thankless prep that happens before you even turn on the stove. The grocery shopping. The washing. The peeling. The dicing. That's the work that makes people order takeout on a Tuesday night, even when they'd rather be cooking.

Our prep kitchens operate in a hub-and-spoke model, sourcing from local farms and suppliers within 100 miles of each facility. Ingredients are prepped to order — never sitting in a warehouse — and delivered in compostable packaging designed to go straight into your fridge's organization system.

We believe cooking should feel like the best part of your day, not a chore you're guilted into. Mise removes the drudgery so you can skip straight to the sizzle.
marketResearch:
The US meal kit market is worth $11.6B in 2025 but facing significant headwinds: churn rates exceed 70% annually, with the top complaint being lack of recipe flexibility and high per-serving costs. Meanwhile, the broader prepared food and grocery delivery market is $68B and growing at 12% CAGR, indicating strong demand for food convenience solutions that don't follow the rigid subscription model.

Mise targets the underserved segment of engaged home cooks — people who watch cooking content, own good knives, and cook 3-5 times per week but are frustrated by prep time. This demographic represents roughly 28 million US households with a combined spending potential of $8.4B on cooking convenience products. Our initial SOM focuses on metropolitan areas with dense populations of food-engaged millennials and Gen-X households, starting with the Northeast corridor — approximately $420M.

Direct competitors are few: traditional meal kits (HelloFresh, Blue Apron) compete on recipe curation, not prep convenience. Grocery delivery (Instacart, Amazon Fresh) delivers whole ingredients. Local prep services exist in scattered markets but lack technology platforms and scale. Mise's moat is our proprietary ingredient parsing engine that breaks any recipe into a prep manifest, combined with a hub-spoke kitchen network optimized for day-of prep and delivery.

Beta results from our Brooklyn pilot show 4.1 orders per month per active user (vs. 2.2 for meal kits), average order value of $38, and a 6-month retention rate of 61%. Customer acquisition cost is $22, driven primarily by organic social content from users sharing their cooking experiences — a viral loop that meal kits rarely achieve because the food looks the same for every subscriber.

name: Grazer
tagline: Regenerative meat from ranchers who are healing the land
description: Grazer is a direct-to-consumer marketplace connecting consumers with ranchers practicing verified regenerative agriculture. Every cut is traceable to a specific ranch, verified by third-party soil health data, and shipped frozen to your door. We prove that the meat you eat can be part of the climate solution.
mission:
The meat industry has a trust problem. Consumers are told to eat less meat to save the planet — and for commodity feedlot beef, that's fair. But the conversation ignores an inconvenient truth: well-managed grazing is one of the most powerful tools we have for rebuilding soil carbon, restoring grassland ecosystems, and reversing desertification. The problem isn't cows. It's how we manage them.

Grazer exists to connect people who care about the land with ranchers who are actively healing it. Every ranch on our platform practices adaptive multi-paddock grazing, maintains year-round ground cover, and submits to annual third-party soil health testing. We don't just claim regenerative — we measure it, publish the data, and let the soil tell the story.

We're building the marketplace that regenerative ranching has always needed. These ranchers produce exceptional meat — animals that spend their lives on grass, moving across diverse pastures, building topsoil with every step. But most of them are stuck selling into commodity markets that pay the same price regardless of how the land is managed. Grazer gives them a direct channel to consumers willing to pay fair prices for food that's part of the solution.

Our platform handles everything the rancher shouldn't have to: e-commerce, cold chain logistics, cut sheet management, customer acquisition, and the soil verification that gives buyers confidence. We take a 15% platform fee and pass the rest to the rancher — roughly 2-3x what they'd earn through conventional channels.

We believe that what you eat is the most powerful environmental vote you cast. Grazer makes it easy to vote for a food system that regenerates rather than extracts.
marketResearch:
The US grass-fed and regenerative meat market is valued at $4.8B in 2025, growing at 18% CAGR — roughly 3x the growth rate of conventional meat. Consumer willingness to pay a premium for verified sustainability claims has increased 42% since 2021, driven by Gen Z and millennial households. The broader DTC meat market (including all premium proteins) is $8.2B.

Grazer's SAM is the regenerative-verified segment: consumers who specifically seek soil-health-verified, ranch-traceable meat. This segment is approximately $1.4B and growing rapidly. Our initial SOM targets environmentally conscious households in major metro areas with high organic food spending — roughly $180M across 15 metro regions.

Competitors include ButcherBox (DTC meat subscription, $600M revenue, but no regenerative verification), Crowd Cow (marketplace model with ranch stories but limited soil data), and White Oak Pastures (single-ranch DTC, gold standard but not a marketplace). Grazer's differentiation is the verification layer: third-party soil health data published per ranch, creating a trust moat that storytelling alone cannot replicate. No competitor currently offers quantified, transparent soil carbon data at the individual ranch level.

Pilot data from 12 partner ranches shows a $142 average order value, 38% repeat purchase rate within 90 days, and NPS of 74. Rancher earnings average 2.4x commodity prices, which drives supply-side retention of 96%. Our challenge is cold chain unit economics — we've partnered with regional processing facilities and use consolidated shipping windows to reduce per-order fulfillment cost to $11.40, approaching profitability at current volumes.

faqs.answer: Grass-fed only means the animal ate grass. It says nothing about soil health, land management, or environmental impact. Grazer ranches are verified for regenerative outcomes — measured soil carbon, water infiltration, and biodiversity. We publish the data.

faqs.question: Is regenerative grazing actually good for the environment?
faqs.answer: When properly managed, adaptive grazing builds topsoil, sequesters carbon, restores water cycles, and increases biodiversity. Multiple peer-reviewed studies show well-managed grasslands can be net carbon sinks. Our ranch data confirms this.

faqs.answer: Orders ship Monday-Wednesday in insulated boxes with dry ice. Everything arrives frozen solid. Most customers dedicate a freezer section and order monthly. Free shipping on orders over $125.

name: Ferment
description: Ferment builds IoT monitoring systems for craft fermentation — from kombucha brewers and sauerkraut producers to craft breweries and artisan cheese makers. Our wireless sensors track pH, temperature, CO2, and microbial activity in real-time, turning the art of fermentation into a repeatable science without losing the craft.
mission:
Fermentation is the oldest biotechnology on earth, and it's experiencing a massive renaissance. Kombucha is a $4B industry. Craft beer keeps growing despite consolidation. Fermented foods line every grocery aisle. But the producers behind this boom — the small-batch brewers, the artisan pickle makers, the garage hot sauce brands — are still monitoring their ferments the same way humans have for centuries: by tasting, smelling, and hoping.

Ferment was founded by a former brewery quality manager and an embedded systems engineer who met at a fermentation festival. The brewery manager was tired of losing $3,000 batches to temperature swings overnight. The engineer was tired of building IoT sensors for applications that didn't matter. Together, they realized fermentation monitoring was a perfect collision of urgent need and available technology.

Our wireless sensor pods attach to any fermentation vessel — from a 5-gallon carboy to a 200-barrel brite tank. They continuously monitor pH, temperature, dissolved CO2, and pressure, streaming data to a dashboard that tracks every ferment against your target profiles. When conditions drift, you get an alert before your batch is compromised.

But we're building more than monitoring hardware. Ferment's real value is the fermentation intelligence platform. Every batch you track builds a dataset that our models use to predict outcomes, suggest adjustments, and help you nail consistency across production runs. For craft producers, consistency is the difference between a farmers market hobby and a scalable business.

We believe the future of food is fermented, and the producers leading that future deserve tools as sophisticated as their craft.
marketResearch:
The global fermented food and beverage market reached $762B in 2025, growing at 8.5% CAGR. The craft segment — small-batch producers making premium fermented products — represents approximately $48B and is growing at 14% CAGR. These producers range from kombucha brands and craft breweries to artisan cheese makers and specialty vinegar producers, creating a diverse but underserved market for production technology.

Ferment's TAM is the fermentation monitoring and quality control segment, estimated at $2.1B globally. Our SAM focuses on craft-scale producers (annual revenue $100K-$20M) in North America and Europe — approximately $680M. The initial SOM targets US craft breweries, kombucha producers, and fermented food startups, representing $95M in near-term opportunity.

The competitive landscape is fragmented. Large-scale fermentation monitoring (Hach, Hamilton) serves industrial breweries and biotech at $50K+ per installation. Consumer-grade tools (Tilt hydrometer, Inkbird temperature controllers) are cheap but limited to single-metric monitoring. Precision Fermentation (a UK startup) and BrewMonitor (US) are the closest competitors, but both focus exclusively on beer. Ferment differentiates by supporting all fermentation types — beer, kombucha, sauerkraut, cheese, vinegar, hot sauce, miso — with cross-category fermentation models that improve predictions across the entire platform.

Pilot data from 68 producers shows 73% reduction in batch failures, average payback period of 2.3 months, and a sensor attachment rate of 3.4 vessels per customer within 6 months of first purchase. Monthly software subscription retention is 91%.

faqs.answer: 6-12 months depending on sampling frequency. Sensors in long-duration ferments (vinegar, miso) can be set to sample every 30 minutes and last a full year. Standard 15-minute sampling gives 6 months.

faqs.question: I make multiple fermented products. Can I use one system?

name: Canteen
tagline: Corporate dining that employees actually want — with zero waste
description: Canteen is a corporate cafeteria management platform that uses predictive ordering, dynamic menus, and real-time waste tracking to transform workplace dining. We help companies serve better food, reduce waste by 60%+, and turn the cafeteria from a cost center into an employee retention tool.
mission:
Corporate cafeterias are broken in a way that everyone sees but nobody fixes. Employees complain the food is boring. Finance complains it's expensive. Sustainability teams are horrified by the waste. And the food service operators caught in the middle are running on spreadsheets and intuition, overproducing by 30-40% because running out is worse than throwing away.

Canteen exists to solve all of these problems simultaneously — because they're actually the same problem. Bad cafeterias waste food because they don't know what employees want. They serve boring menus because they have no feedback loop. They're expensive because waste and dissatisfaction compound into a cycle that nobody has the data to break.

Our platform integrates with a company's existing food service operation — whether that's an in-house kitchen, a contract caterer, or a mix. We provide demand prediction (what will employees actually eat today?), dynamic menu optimization (what should we serve based on historical preferences, dietary needs, and seasonal ingredients?), and real-time waste tracking (how much went uneaten and why?).

The result is cafeterias that serve food employees choose over DoorDash, waste 60% less food, and cost 25% less to operate. For companies competing for talent in return-to-office mandates, a great cafeteria is no longer a perk — it's a retention strategy. Nobody admits that lunch is a reason they come to the office, but the data says otherwise.

We're building the operating system for workplace dining — starting with the 50,000 corporate cafeterias in North America that collectively serve 30 million meals a day and waste a quarter of them.
marketResearch:
The US corporate food service market is valued at $28B in 2025, with contract catering (Aramark, Sodexo, Compass Group) controlling 70% of the market. Food waste in corporate cafeterias averages 30-40% of total production, representing $8-11B in annual waste. Meanwhile, 78% of companies cite food and dining as a top-5 factor in return-to-office employee satisfaction surveys.

Canteen's TAM is the corporate food service technology market — approximately $3.2B globally. Our SAM focuses on US companies with 500+ employees operating on-site dining facilities, representing approximately $1.1B. Our initial SOM targets technology companies and financial services firms in major metro areas — the sectors most aggressively investing in workplace experience — at roughly $160M.

The competitive landscape is dominated by legacy food service management software (FoodPro, Caterease) built for operations, not optimization. Leanpath leads in waste tracking hardware but lacks demand prediction or menu optimization. Winnow offers AI-powered waste monitoring for commercial kitchens but doesn't address the demand side. Canteen is the only platform that closes the loop: predict demand, optimize the menu, track waste, and feed the data back into tomorrow's predictions.

Pilot results from 4 corporate campuses (combined 8,200 daily diners) show 63% waste reduction, 28% increase in employee dining participation (vs. ordering delivery), and 22% decrease in per-meal food cost. Contract is $2-4 per employee per month, with ROI typically positive within 45 days through waste reduction alone.

name: Honeycomb
tagline: Healthy bees, healthy harvests. Monitored hive by hive.
description: Honeycomb builds in-hive monitoring systems that track colony health in real-time. Our non-invasive sensors measure temperature, humidity, acoustic patterns, weight, and bee traffic — detecting disease, queen loss, swarming risk, and nutritional stress before visible symptoms appear. Built for commercial beekeepers and pollination services managing hundreds of hives.
mission:
One in three bites of food depends on pollination, and honeybees do the heavy lifting. But bee colony losses have averaged 40% annually for the past decade, and commercial beekeepers are burning out trying to keep pace. A single beekeeper might manage 2,000 hives spread across hundreds of miles. The only way they know a colony is in trouble is by opening the hive and looking — a process that's slow, stressful for the bees, and impossible to do at the frequency needed across large operations.

Honeycomb changes this equation entirely. Our sensor package slides into the hive body without disturbing the colony. It continuously monitors five critical dimensions of hive health: internal temperature patterns (which reveal brood health and thermoregulation), humidity (linked to disease risk), acoustic signatures (which can detect queen loss, swarming intent, and colony stress), hive weight (tracking food stores and foraging success), and entrance traffic (measuring the daily rhythm of a healthy colony).

We built Honeycomb because we saw an industry desperate for better tools. Commercial beekeepers are losing 30-50% of their colonies annually, each colony replacement costing $150-200. Pollination contracts — worth $20B globally — depend on delivering healthy colonies to farms at precisely the right time. The beekeeper who knows a colony is struggling three weeks before it collapses can intervene. The one who finds out at the next inspection often can't.

Our platform aggregates data across entire operations, flagging the hives that need attention and letting beekeepers prioritize their limited field time. Instead of opening every hive on a two-week rotation, they can focus on the 15% that actually need intervention — and often catch problems that a visual inspection would miss entirely.

We're not replacing the beekeeper's skill and intuition. We're extending it across thousands of hives simultaneously.
marketResearch:
The global beekeeping industry is valued at $11.3B in 2025, with the commercial segment (500+ hives) representing $6.8B. Annual colony losses cost the US beekeeping industry approximately $2.4B in replacement and lost productivity. The pollination services market alone is $8.2B globally and growing at 9% CAGR, driven by increasing agricultural demand for managed pollination.

Honeycomb's TAM is the precision beekeeping technology market, estimated at $1.8B globally. Our SAM focuses on commercial beekeepers (500+ hives) and pollination service providers in North America, Europe, and Australia — approximately $540M. Our initial SOM targets US commercial operations managing 1,000+ hives, representing $72M in immediate opportunity.

Competitors include Arnia (UK, academic-origin hive monitoring), BeeHero (Israel, $40M raised, focused on pollination analytics), and Broodminder (US, hobbyist-scale weight monitoring). BeeHero is the primary competitive threat but focuses on the pollination analytics layer rather than colony health intervention. Honeycomb's differentiation is the multi-sensor fusion approach — combining acoustic, thermal, weight, humidity, and traffic data to detect problems 2-3 weeks earlier than any single-metric system. Our acoustic models for queen loss detection have 94% accuracy, vs. 60-70% for competitors relying on temperature alone.

Beta deployment across 4 commercial operations (6,200 hives total) shows 31% reduction in colony losses, 22% fewer field inspection trips, and estimated annual savings of $84 per monitored hive. At $12/hive/month ($144/year), the ROI is immediately clear. Beekeepers report that the queen loss alerts alone justify the subscription.

name: Steep
tagline: Single-origin tea, curated and delivered to your cup
description: Steep is a single-origin tea subscription that connects tea drinkers directly with small-estate growers in China, Japan, India, and Taiwan. Each monthly shipment features two teas with detailed origin stories, brewing guides, and tasting notes — plus a community of tea enthusiasts exploring the world's most nuanced beverage together.
mission:
The specialty coffee revolution proved that people will pay more for quality, traceability, and story. Tea — a beverage with deeper history, wider variety, and more nuanced flavor — deserves the same revolution. But while coffee has its third wave, tea in the West is still largely stuck in the dark ages: commodity tea bags from anonymous blends, priced by the pound with no regard for origin, cultivar, or craft.

Steep exists to be tea's third wave. We work directly with small-estate growers — families who have tended the same gardens for generations in Yunnan, Shizuoka, Darjeeling, and Alishan. We buy at prices that reflect the quality of their work (2-4x commodity rates), and we tell their stories with the respect they deserve.

Every tea we source is single-origin, single-harvest, and selected by our tasting team in blind evaluations. We don't carry a permanent catalog — our selections change with the seasons because the best teas are seasonal by nature. A first-flush Darjeeling in April. A new-harvest sencha in May. An aged pu-erh that only appears when a family decides to release a limited pressing.

Our subscription is designed for discovery. Each month, members receive two teas they've never tried — enough to brew 30+ cups — with detailed tasting notes, brewing parameters, and the story behind each garden. Our community platform lets members share their experiences, compare notes, and go deeper into the world of tea.

We believe tea is the most underappreciated luxury in the world. Steep is making it accessible to people who care about quality, origin, and the craft behind their cup.
marketResearch:
The global specialty tea market reached $8.2B in 2025, growing at 11% CAGR — significantly outpacing the broader $72B tea market. In the US, premium and specialty tea sales grew 18% year-over-year, driven by health-conscious millennials and Gen Z consumers seeking alternatives to coffee. The subscription box market for food and beverage is $12.4B, with tea subscriptions representing a fast-growing niche.

Steep's TAM is the US specialty tea market at $3.1B. Our SAM — consumers willing to pay $30+/month for curated, single-origin tea subscriptions — is approximately $480M. Our initial SOM targets the specialty coffee crossover demographic (people who already pay for quality beans and are curious about tea) in urban markets, representing $62M.

Competitors include Ippodo (traditional Japanese tea, DTC but limited curation), Harney & Sons (broad catalog, not single-origin focused), Yunnan Sourcing (enthusiast marketplace, no curation), and Tea Runners (subscription box, but blends rather than single-origin). Steep differentiates through the curation layer: our blind-tasting process, seasonal rotation, and deep origin stories create an experience closer to a wine club than a tea shop. No competitor currently combines direct-sourcing transparency, seasonal single-origin curation, and community in a single platform.

Beta results from 2,800 subscribers show 14-month average subscriber lifetime, 71% gift conversion rate (members gifting subscriptions), and a monthly churn rate of 4.2%. Average revenue per subscriber is $38/month with 62% gross margins after sourcing, fulfillment, and shipping. Our strongest acquisition channel is member referrals (34% of new signups), indicating strong product-market fit.

name: Provision
tagline: AI meal planning for families who can't eat everything
description: Provision is an AI meal planning platform built specifically for families managing dietary restrictions. Whether it's celiac, nut allergies, dairy-free kids, diabetic grandparents, or a mix of all four — Provision creates weekly meal plans that work for everyone at the table, generates unified grocery lists, and integrates with delivery services.
mission:
Meal planning is hard enough for a family with no dietary restrictions. Now imagine planning for a household where one child has celiac disease, another is allergic to tree nuts, dad is managing type 2 diabetes, and mom is dairy-free by choice. Every single meal becomes a puzzle: What can everyone eat? What substitutions work? How do I make one dinner, not four?

Provision was born in a kitchen like this. Our founder is a parent of two kids with food allergies who spent years planning meals on spreadsheets, cross-referencing ingredient lists, and crying in the grocery store aisle trying to remember which bread brand is safe for both children. She realized that this problem — feeding a family with mixed dietary needs — was universal, exhausting, and completely unsolved by existing meal planning apps.

Every existing meal planning tool assumes everyone at the table eats the same thing. Provision doesn't. Our AI understands the constraints of each family member, finds meals that satisfy all of them, and when that's not possible, suggests smart modifications — like making the pasta dish with a side of regular bread for the non-celiac members and a safe alternative for everyone else.

We generate complete weekly meal plans (breakfast, lunch, dinner, snacks), produce unified grocery lists that can be sent directly to Instacart, Walmart Grocery, or Amazon Fresh, and track nutritional intake to ensure restricted diets remain nutritionally complete. For families managing medical conditions, we integrate with dietitians who can review and approve plans.

Feeding your family shouldn't feel like solving an optimization problem. Provision solves it for you so dinner can just be dinner again.
marketResearch:
Approximately 32 million Americans have food allergies, and 3.1 million follow a gluten-free diet for celiac disease. When expanded to include dietary preferences (vegetarian, vegan, keto), religious restrictions, and medical diets (diabetic, low-FODMAP), an estimated 45% of US households manage at least one dietary restriction. The meal planning app market is $1.2B in 2025, growing at 16% CAGR, but no market leader specifically addresses multi-restriction families.

Provision's TAM is the intersection of meal planning and dietary management — approximately $2.8B when including associated grocery delivery integration revenue. Our SAM focuses on US families managing two or more dietary restrictions within a single household — roughly 18 million households representing $860M in annual spending on meal planning tools and related services. Our initial SOM targets digitally active families with children who have diagnosed food allergies, approximately $110M.

Competitors include Mealime (general meal planning, basic filter options), Eat This Much (calorie-focused, individual-oriented), and Yummly (recipe discovery, owned by Whirlpool). None handle multi-person, multi-restriction household planning. The closest analogs are registered dietitian services ($150-300/month) which are prohibitively expensive for most families. Provision fills this gap at $14.99/month for a family plan — less than a single dietitian consultation.

Beta results from 4,200 families show 89% weekly active usage (planning meals for the upcoming week), average time savings of 3.2 hours per week on meal planning and grocery shopping, and a 4.8/5 satisfaction rating from families with 3+ dietary restrictions. Monthly churn is 3.1%, significantly below the 8% industry average for meal planning apps, indicating strong product-market fit in the multi-restriction niche.

name: Sprout
tagline: Vertical farming kits that grow your menu year-round
description: Sprout builds modular indoor vertical farming systems designed for restaurants, hotels, and food service operations. Our climate-controlled growing towers produce fresh herbs, microgreens, and leafy greens on-site — cutting supply chain costs, eliminating food miles, and giving chefs a living pantry steps from their kitchen.
mission:
Every restaurant in America receives a produce delivery that traveled an average of 1,500 miles. By the time those herbs reach the kitchen, they've lost half their flavor and most of their shelf life. Chefs know this. They compensate by over-ordering, accepting waste, and making do with whatever survived the supply chain.

Sprout changes that equation by putting the farm inside the restaurant. Our vertical growing towers fit in a closet, a hallway, a corner of the prep kitchen, or a dedicated grow room. They produce a continuous harvest of herbs, microgreens, and leafy greens — basil, cilantro, mint, arugula, specialty microgreens, edible flowers — with zero pesticides, zero food miles, and flavor that makes the delivered stuff taste like cardboard.

We designed Sprout specifically for food service operations, not home hobbyists. Our systems are built for reliability (sealed climate control, automated nutrient dosing, LED grow lights tuned for flavor compounds), volume (enough production to meaningfully offset a restaurant's herb and greens purchasing), and ease of use (a line cook can manage the system — no horticulture degree required).

The economics work because the alternative is terrible. Restaurants spend $8-15 per pound on fresh herbs that are already wilting. Sprout produces the same herbs for under $2 per pound, harvested minutes before service. Our customers typically see full payback on hardware within 8-12 months, after which the ongoing cost is just nutrients, water, and electricity.

We believe the future of restaurant produce is hyper-local — not farm-to-table, but wall-to-table. Sprout is building the infrastructure to make that possible for every kitchen, not just the ones with rooftop gardens and six-figure budgets.

name: Forage
tagline: Wild ingredients and rare finds for ambitious kitchens
description: Forage is a B2B marketplace connecting professional chefs with wild food foragers, specialty growers, and artisan producers. From ramps and morels to high-altitude honey and heritage grain flours — Forage makes the rare and seasonal ingredients that define exceptional cuisine available on demand, with full traceability and sustainable sourcing verification.
mission:
The best restaurants in the world are defined by their ingredients. Not just quality — specificity. The morels from a particular forest in Oregon. The sea beans harvested on a specific stretch of Maine coastline. The heritage wheat milled by a family in Kansas. These ingredients create dishes that can't be replicated, menus that tell stories, and dining experiences that justify the trip.

But sourcing these ingredients is a nightmare. Chefs spend hours texting foragers, calling small farms, and chasing down artisan producers who don't have websites. Supply is unpredictable. Quality varies. Logistics are improvised. The chef who finds an incredible ingredient this week might not be able to get it again for months — or ever.

Forage solves this by building the marketplace that wild and specialty ingredients have never had. We connect a vetted network of foragers, specialty growers, and artisan producers with professional kitchens — providing real-time inventory, sustainable sourcing verification, cold chain logistics, and the reliability that chefs need to put an ingredient on a menu with confidence.

Our sourcing standards are non-negotiable. Every forager on our platform follows sustainable harvest guidelines verified by our field team. Every specialty grower meets our quality benchmarks. Every artisan producer is vetted for food safety compliance. We're not just a marketplace — we're a trust layer for an industry that has always run on relationships and handshakes.

We believe that the best food comes from the most dedicated producers. Forage makes their ingredients accessible to every ambitious kitchen — not just the ones with a Rolodex full of forager phone numbers.
marketResearch:
The US specialty and artisan food ingredient market is estimated at $18.4B in 2025, growing at 13% CAGR. The wild-harvested and foraged food segment specifically is approximately $1.8B, driven by the fine dining and new American cuisine movements that prioritize hyper-local and seasonal sourcing. The broader restaurant specialty purchasing market — ingredients not available through mainstream distributors — represents $6.2B.

Forage's TAM is the specialty ingredient sourcing market for professional kitchens, approximately $6.2B in the US. Our SAM focuses on fine dining, chef-driven restaurants, and boutique hotels that actively source wild and specialty ingredients — approximately $1.4B. Our initial SOM targets Michelin-starred and James Beard-recognized restaurants, destination dining concepts, and high-end hotel restaurants in 15 metro markets, representing $120M.

The competitive landscape is highly fragmented. Specialty distributors (Baldor, Sid Wainer) carry some specialty items but lack wild-foraged depth and real-time seasonal inventory. Direct forager relationships (the current standard) are unreliable and unscalable. Regalis Foods (NYC) is the closest analog — a specialty distributor focused on truffles and luxury ingredients — but operates as a traditional distributor rather than a marketplace. Forage's differentiation is the marketplace model: real-time seasonal availability from a distributed network of 200+ foragers and producers, with sustainability verification and cold chain logistics as platform services.

Beta results from 85 restaurant partners show an average order value of $380, 3.2 orders per month per active account, and a 92% ingredient quality satisfaction rating. Supply-side retention is 94% — foragers and producers earn 75% of the sale price (vs. 40-50% through traditional distribution). The seasonal nature of our inventory drives urgency-based purchasing patterns with strong email open rates (48%) for new availability alerts.

faqs.question: Is Forage only for fine dining?
faqs.answer: No. While many of our early partners are fine dining, we serve any professional kitchen that values ingredient quality — including fast-casual concepts, bakeries, cocktail bars, and hotel restaurants. We verify all accounts to ensure food safety compliance.

faqs.question: How do you verify sustainable sourcing?
faqs.answer: Every forager on our platform follows published sustainable harvest guidelines specific to their region and species. Our field team conducts annual on-site verification. We limit harvest volumes per forager per species to prevent overharvesting. Full traceability documentation accompanies every order.

faqs.question: What if an ingredient I want isn't available?
faqs.answer: Set up alerts for any ingredient. When it becomes available — whether that's morel season starting or a producer releasing a limited batch — you'll get an email or text notification. You can also post sourcing requests visible to our forager and producer network.

faqs.question: What are your minimums?
faqs.answer: No order minimums. We understand that wild and specialty ingredients are used in small quantities. Average order is $380 but we regularly fulfill orders as small as $45. Free shipping on orders over $200.
